info.title: IPGeolocation.io: User Agent API
info.description:
Parse browser, device, and operating system details from a User Agent string.
The API also detects crawlers, bots, and potential attackers based on anomalies
in the user agent string.

Two endpoints are available, supporting three usage modes:

- **`GET /v3/user-agent`** supports two modes: don't set a custom `User-Agent`
  header to parse the caller's own user agent (browsers and most HTTP clients send
  one automatically), or pass any string in the `User-Agent` header to parse it
  explicitly. A request with no `User-Agent` header at all returns HTTP 400.
- **`POST /v3/user-agent`** parses a custom user agent string from a JSON body
  (`uaString` field). Available on paid plans only.
- **`POST /v3/user-agent-bulk`** parses up to 50,000 user agent strings in a
  single request. Available on paid plans only.

User agent data can also be retrieved alongside IP geolocation data via the
`/v3/ipgeo` endpoint using `include=user_agent`.

## Authentication

Two authentication methods are supported:

### API Key

Pass your API key as the `apiKey` query parameter on every request. You can find your
key in the [IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/). Store it in
server-side environment variables. Avoid exposing it in client-side JavaScript.

### Request Origin (CORS)

Available on paid plans only. Whitelist your domain in the dashboard under the
"API Keys" section. Once configured, requests from that domain (and all its subdomains)
are accepted without passing `apiKey`. Enter your root domain (e.g. `example.com`),
not the full URL.

Each plan has a limit on the number of extra API keys and request origins:

| Plan | Extra API Keys + Request Origins |
|---|---|
| Free | 0 |
| Starter | 1 |
| Plus | 2 |
| Pro | 2 |
| Business | 3 |
| Premium | 3 |

Plans are sized by API credits, not requests: Free includes 1,000 credits
per day; Starter 150,000 credits/month; Plus 500,000; Pro 1,000,000;
Business 2,000,000; Premium 5,000,000.

Additional keys or origins can be added for $2.50 per month each.

## Credit Usage

Credits are charged only for successful **HTTP 200** responses. The exact number of
credits consumed by a request is returned in the `X-Credits-Charged` response header.

Each successful user agent lookup costs **1 credit** per user agent string parsed.
For bulk requests, the total credits charged equals the number of user agent strings
submitted.

When using `/v3/ipgeo` with `include=user_agent`, no additional credits are charged
beyond the base IP lookup cost.

## Plan Availability

- **`GET /v3/user-agent`** (auto-detect or explicit `User-Agent` header) is available
  on all plans including Free.
- **`POST /v3/user-agent`** (custom string via JSON body) is available on **paid plans only**.
- **`POST /v3/user-agent-bulk`** is available on **paid plans only**.
- User agent data via `/v3/ipgeo?include=user_agent` is available on **paid plans only**.

## Response Formats

The API supports JSON (default) and XML output.

- Set the `output` query parameter to `json` or `xml`.
- Alternatively, set the `Accept` header to `application/json`, `application/xml`,
  or `text/xml`.

If neither is specified, the response is returned as JSON. XML responses use a
`LinkedHashMap` root element (an `ArrayList` of them for bulk requests).

## Parameter Name Casing

Query parameter names are case-sensitive. Use exact names such as
`apiKey` and `output`.

get.summary: Parse user agent string (auto-detect or explicit header)
get.description:
Parses a user agent string and returns browser, device, and operating system
details. Also detects bots, crawlers, and malicious or malformed user agent strings.

This endpoint supports two usage modes:

**Mode 1 — Caller's own user agent:**
Don't set a custom `User-Agent` header. Browsers and most HTTP clients send one
automatically, and the API parses it. If the request carries no `User-Agent`
header at all, the API returns HTTP 400.

**Mode 2 — Explicit user agent header:**
Pass any user agent string in the `User-Agent` request header. The API parses
that string instead of detecting the caller's own user agent. Use this to
simulate or test specific user agent strings server-side.

Each successful lookup consumes **1 credit**.

parameters.name: User-Agent
parameters.description:
The user agent string to parse. Browsers and most HTTP clients send their own
`User-Agent` header automatically, so by default the caller's own user agent is
parsed. Set it to any string to parse that string instead. If the request has
no `User-Agent` header at all, the API returns HTTP 400.
parameters.example: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 6.0.1; Nexus 5X Build/MMB29P) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/41.0.2272.96 Mobile Safari/537.36 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)

200.description: Parsed user agent details for the resolved user agent string.

X-Credits-Charged.description: Number of API credits consumed by this request.

example.user_agent_string: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_11_2) AppleWebKit/601.3.9 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/9.0.2 Safari/601.3.9
example.name: Safari

application/xml.example:
<LinkedHashMap>
  <user_agent_string>Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_11_2) AppleWebKit/601.3.9 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/9.0.2 Safari/601.3.9</user_agent_string>
  <name>Safari</name>
  <type>Browser</type>
  <version>9.0.2</version>
  <version_major>9</version_major>
  <device>
      <name>Apple Macintosh</name>
      <type>Desktop</type>
      <brand>Apple</brand>
      <cpu>Intel</cpu>
  </device>
  <engine>
      <name>AppleWebKit</name>
      <type>Browser</type>
      <version>601.3.9</version>
      <version_major>601</version_major>
  </engine>
  <operating_system>
      <name>Mac OS</name>
      <type>Desktop</type>
      <version>10.11.2</version>
      <version_major>10.11</version_major>
      <build>??</build>
  </operating_system>
</LinkedHashMap>

post.description:
Parses a custom user agent string supplied in the JSON request body and returns
browser, device, and operating system details.

**Mode 3 — Custom user agent string via POST body:**
Pass the user agent string as the `uaString` field in a JSON payload. This is
intended for server-side use cases where the string to be parsed is different
from the caller's own user agent and is known at request time.

This endpoint is available on **paid plans only**.

Each successful lookup consumes **1 credit**.

post.description:
Parses up to **50,000 user agent strings** in a single request.

Pass a JSON body containing the `uaStrings` array. Each entry is parsed as sent.
A `null` or blank entry fails the whole request with HTTP 400
(`'userAgentString' must not be empty or null`) and nothing is charged. The total
credits charged equals the number of strings in the array.

This endpoint is available on **paid plans only**.

requestBody.description: JSON body containing the array of user agent strings to parse.

uaStrings.description:
Array of user agent strings to parse. Maximum 50,000 entries per request.
A `null` or blank entry fails the whole request with HTTP 400. An empty
array is not an error: it returns HTTP 200 with `[]` and 0 credits.
example: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 8.0.0; SM-G960F Build/R16NW) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/62.0.3202.84 Mobile Safari/537.36
Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux armv7l like Android; en-us) AppleWebKit/531.2+ (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/5.0 Safari/533.2+ Kindle/3.0+
Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; U; en-US) AppleWebKit/528.5+ (KHTML, like Gecko, Safari/528.5+) Version/4.0 Kindle/3.0 (screen 600x800; rotate)

200.description:
Array of parsed user agent results, one object per submitted string,
in the same order as the input array.

X-Credits-Charged.description:
Total number of API credits consumed by this request.
Equals the number of user agent strings submitted.

ApiKey.name: apiKey
ApiKey.description:
Your IPGeolocation API key. Required unless Request Origin (CORS) authentication
is configured for your domain on a paid plan. Get your key from the
[IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/).

Output.name: output
Output.description:
Desired response format. Defaults to `json` if not specified. You can also
control the format using the `Accept` header (`application/json`,
`application/xml`, or `text/xml`). For successful responses and authentication
errors, the `Accept` header takes precedence if both are provided: `output` is
used only when the `Accept` header is absent or set to `*/*`, and an `Accept`
value other than `application/xml` or `text/xml` (for example a browser's
default) returns JSON even with `output=xml`. Values are matched exactly (use
lowercase `xml`).

If `output` is unknown or unsupported, it is ignored and the response defaults
to JSON (`application/json`) with HTTP 200.

BadRequest.description:
Bad Request. Returned for one of the following reasons:
- Special characters [ ] { } | ^ ` are passed in the API URL (either in parameters or values), especially in the API key.
- The `uaString` is empty or null when calling `/v3/user-agent`(POST).
- The request body is not valid JSON (`Malformed JSON request or invalid field`)
  when calling `/v3/user-agent`(POST).
- No `User-Agent` header is present when calling `GET /v3/user-agent`. Unlike the
  POST body, there is no alternative way to supply the string for this call, so a
  missing/blank header always fails validation.

Request body validation (malformed JSON, a missing or blank `uaString`) runs before
the API key is checked.

value.message: Invalid character found in the request target.

emptyUaString.summary: Empty or null user agent string

value.message: User-Agent string must not be blank
'userAgentString' must not be empty or null

malformedJson.summary: Request body is not valid JSON

value.message: Malformed JSON request or invalid field

BadRequestBulk.description:
Bad Request. Returned for one of the following reasons:
- Special characters [ ] { } | ^ ` are passed in the API URL (either in parameters or values), especially in the API key.
- The JSON body has no `uaStrings` field (or it is `null`). An empty array is not
  an error: it returns HTTP 200 with `[]` and 0 credits.
- The `uaStrings` array contains a `null` or blank entry
  (`'userAgentString' must not be empty or null`). The whole request fails and
  nothing is charged.
- More than 50,000 user agent strings are provided in a single bulk request.
- The request body is not valid JSON (`Malformed JSON request or invalid field`) or
  `uaStrings` is not a JSON array of strings.

Request body validation (malformed JSON, a missing `uaStrings` field, more than
50,000 entries) runs before the API key is checked.

value.message: Invalid character found in the request target.
User-Agent strings for bulk lookup are missing

blankBulkEntry.summary: Null or blank entry in uaStrings

value.message: 'userAgentString' must not be empty or null

malformedJson.summary: Request body is not valid JSON

value.message: Malformed JSON request or invalid field

uaStringsNotArray.summary: uaStrings is not a JSON array of strings

value.message: 'uaStrings' must be a JSON array of strings, e.g. {"uaStrings": ["value1", "value2"]}

bulkLimitExceeded.summary: More than 50,000 strings in bulk request

value.message: No. of lookup queries cannot be more than 50000

Unauthorized.description:
Unauthorized. Returned for one of the following reasons:
- An API key is required for this request, but the `apiKey` query parameter is missing and the request doesn't come from a domain added under Request Origin.
- The provided API key is not valid, or the request has no API key and its `Origin` or `Referer` domain is not registered as a Request Origin.
- The request is made using an API key of a database subscription.
- The account's email address has not been verified.
- The account has been locked due to abuse or illegal activity.
- Requests are made after the subscription trial has expired.
- The subscription is paused.
- `POST /v3/user-agent` (custom user agent string in the request body) is called
  using a free subscription API key.

NotFound.description: Not Found. Returned when an invalid or non-existent endpoint is called.

MethodNotAllowed.description:
Method Not Allowed. Returned when an unsupported HTTP method is used.

- `/v3/user-agent` supports GET and POST.
- `/v3/user-agent-bulk` supports POST only.

value.message: Request method 'GET' is not supported

ContentTooLarge.description:
Content Too Large. Returned when the POST request payload exceeds
the allowed size limit.

text/html.example:
413 Request Entity Too Large

nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu)

UnsupportedMediaType.description:
Unsupported Media Type. Returned when the `Content-Type` header is not
set to `application/json` for POST requests to:
- `/v3/user-agent`
- `/v3/user-agent-bulk`

TooManyRequests.description:
Too Many Requests. Returned for one of the following reasons:
- The API credit allowance has been reached for a free subscription.
- The API credit allowance has been reached for an active trial subscription (capped at 100,000 API credits).
- The API credit allowance has been reached for a paid subscription with surcharge usage disabled.
- The API credit allowance has been reached for a paid subscription with status 'past due' or 'deleted'.
- The surcharge (overage) credit limit has been reached.

ClientClosedRequest.description:
Client Closed Request. Returned when the client sets a very short timeout,
causing the connection to close before the server responds (logged by the
edge proxy; the client receives no response). Increase the timeout on the
client side.

InternalServerError.description:
Internal Server Error. The server encountered an unexpected condition
that prevented it from fulfilling the request. If the issue persists,
contact support@ipgeolocation.io.

example.message: Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again or contact technical support at support@ipgeolocation.io

BadGateway.description:
Bad Gateway. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API, not by the API
application, when it gets an invalid response from the API server. The
response body is set by the proxy. This is usually temporary; retry the
request.

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Service Unavailable. Returned when the API cannot verify your API key (or request
origin) because of a temporary internal error, for example when the billing service
is unreachable and the key has not been verified recently. Keys that were verified
recently keep working. Retry later; if it persists, contact support@ipgeolocation.io.

example.message: We're unable to verify your API key (YOUR_API_KEY) due to an internal error. Please contact technical support for assistance at support@ipgeolocation.io

GatewayTimeout.description:
Gateway Timeout. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API, not by the
API application, when the API server does not respond in time. The response
body is set by the proxy. Retry the request.

HttpVersionNotSupported.description:
HTTP Version Not Supported. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API,
not by the API application, when the request uses an HTTP protocol version
it does not support. The response body is set by the proxy.

PaymentRequired.description:
Payment Required. Returned for a paid (non-Free) subscription whose active-until
date has passed: one day after the active-until date for active or trialing
subscriptions, and from the active-until date for past-due or deleted
subscriptions. It is checked before any usage quota. Paused subscriptions and
expired trials get HTTP 401 instead, and Free plan keys never get 402. Renew or
upgrade the plan to continue using IPGeolocation API.

ErrorResponse.description:
Returned for any non-200 response. Contains only a human-readable `message`.
Message text can vary by status and condition; examples in this spec are
representative, not exhaustive, and should not be treated as stable machine codes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what went wrong. Use HTTP status for control flow.
message.example: User-Agent string must not be blank

UserAgentResponse.description:
Parsed user agent details including browser, device, layout engine, and
operating system information. Also indicates bots, crawlers, or malicious
user agent strings.

user_agent_string.description: The raw user agent string that was parsed.
user_agent_string.example: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_11_2) AppleWebKit/601.3.9 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/9.0.2 Safari/601.3.9

name.description:
Name of the detected agent (e.g. browser name, bot name, or `"Hacker"`
if the string is malformed or contains injected scripts).

type.description: Type of the detected user agent. See possible values in the documentation.

version.description: Full version string of the detected agent.

version_major.description: Major version of the detected agent.

Device.description: Hardware device information extracted from the user agent string.

name.description: Name of the device (e.g. model name or manufacturer).

type.description: Type of the device. See possible values in the documentation.

brand.description: Brand or manufacturer of the device.

cpu.description: CPU architecture or model of the device. May be `"Unknown"`.

Engine.description: Layout engine information extracted from the user agent string.

type.description: Type of the layout engine. See possible values in the documentation.

version.description: Full version string of the layout engine. May be `"??"` if unknown.

version_major.description: Major version of the layout engine. May be `"??"` if unknown.

OperatingSystem.description: Operating system information extracted from the user agent string.

type.description: Type of the operating system. See possible values in the documentation.

version.description: Full version string of the operating system. May be `"??"` if unknown.

version_major.description: Major version of the operating system. May be `"??"` if unknown.

build.description: Build identifier of the operating system. May be `"??"` if unknown.

ApiKeyAuth.name: apiKey
ApiKeyAuth.description:
API key passed as the `apiKey` query parameter. Get yours from the
[IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/). For client-side
usage, consider using Request Origin (CORS) authentication instead to
avoid exposing your key.

tags.name: User Agent
tags.description:
API endpoints for parsing user agent strings into browser, device, layout engine,
and operating system details. Supports single lookups via request header, custom
string lookups via JSON body, and bulk parsing of up to 50,000 strings per request.
Also detects bots, crawlers, and malicious or malformed user agent strings.
